nodes.label: HMD-Authoritative Smooth-Turn Sign/Gain Calibration Saga
nodes.rationale: Multi-build saga to make player-capsule yaw track HMD-authoritative smooth-turn input: request-based yaw step ignored KEX's real accumulator gain (ratio ~-0.85); observed-KEX-yaw mode overcompensated due to prime/reset bugs; the eventual same-sign fix required separating snap vs smooth pixel-per-degree gain and a distinct kexMouseSign from userSign; final architecture used authViewSign plus display_baseline=smooth_authoritative_kex_delta_display_flip/same_sign to decouple body-turn sign from display-correction sign.
nodes.norm_label: hmd-authoritative smooth-turn sign/gain calibration saga

nodes.label: Selection Bracket Double-Vision / Depth Ghost
nodes.rationale: The VR selection bracket is a single world-locked OpenXR quad, so doubling/shimmering could only occur if it renders at the wrong depth while the eyes converge on the real object (distM jumping 2.8<->21m). Root cause is bad picking/depth placement, not a true stereo double-render.
nodes.norm_label: selection bracket double-vision / depth ghost

nodes.label: Frob: Collision-less Wall-Fixture Selection Saga
nodes.rationale: Small wall fixtures (card slots, switches, keypads) have no own collision, so every ray-based pick passes through them; desktop SS2 instead selects by screen-space cursor proximity. Multiple misdiagnoses (vertical miscalibration, native-picker-calibration) were chased before the true root cause (head-local cursor vs KEX render-camera frame mismatch) was found, fixed via a camera-ray cursor, then finally solved architecturally via a Squirrel world-space semantic scan + engine-frob publish-back.
nodes.norm_label: frob: collision-less wall-fixture selection saga

nodes.label: Frob Misdiagnosis: Vertical Cursor Miscalibration (SUPERSEDED)
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: detection correlated with injected cursor Y, so the fix was believed to be a static aim_flat_fov/offset_y calibration constant. Superseded once world_frob_prefer_native exposed that KEX's native cursor-pick just isn't precise enough for small VR targets, and later that the whole cursor was in the wrong reference frame.
nodes.norm_label: frob misdiagnosis: vertical cursor miscalibration (superseded)

nodes.label: Frob Misdiagnosis: world_frob_prefer_native Cursor-Projection Miscalibration (SUPERSEDED)
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: believed the fix was to trust the raw segment-trace hit point (gated by frobbability) instead of KEX's imprecise screen-cursor pick. Superseded by discovering the true problem was that the frob cursor is projected in head-local space while the scene is rendered from the offset KEX camera -- a reference-frame mismatch, not a precision/gating problem.
nodes.norm_label: frob misdiagnosis: world_frob_prefer_native cursor-projection miscalibration (superseded)

nodes.label: Frob Root Cause: Head-Local Cursor vs KEX Render-Camera Frame Mismatch
nodes.rationale: TRUE ROOT CAUSE. The frob cursor is projected in HEAD-LOCAL space (invHead = conjugate(predicted head orientation)) but the scene is rendered from the KEX camera, which differs from the head by ~21 deg yaw and a pitch sign flip plus pitch_bias_degrees. Any flat calibration offset only worked at one head pose and drifted at others; the fix projects the controller's world-space ray through the same KEX render-camera basis already captured for the bracket.
nodes.norm_label: frob root cause: head-local cursor vs kex render-camera frame mismatch

nodes.label: Frob Fix: Camera-Ray Cursor (aim_camera_ray_cursor)
nodes.rationale: Reprojects the game-world hit point of the controller ray through the render-camera basis (not the head-local basis) to derive the screen cursor, making frob selection head-stable by construction.
nodes.norm_label: frob fix: camera-ray cursor (aim_camera_ray_cursor)

nodes.label: pick_camera_probe: ~16% Residual Head-Coupling Bug
nodes.rationale: pick_camera_probe writes the controller world ray directly into the engine pick-camera, correctly avoiding the 2D-cursor problem, but with the controller physically still, ~16% of head yaw still leaked into the 'fixed' ray because reconstructing R = latestPickBasis*invHMD does not cleanly handle the KEX/OpenXR yaw mirror+offset (kexYaw = -headtrackYaw - 33.6 deg).
nodes.norm_label: pick_camera_probe: ~16% residual head-coupling bug

nodes.label: Squirrel World-Space Frob Scan + Engine-Frob Publish-Back -- CONFIRMED WORKING
nodes.rationale: Final architecture: Squirrel scans all objects scoring by perpendicular distance to the published controller world ray (head/camera-independent), filters by FrobInfo/semantic name hints, publishes the chosen target back via ss2vr_hl, and interact_squirrel_engine_frob writes it into objectUnderCursor/frobTarget so the engine's native USE frobs it with full Frobber context. Resolved the multi-week left-hand world-interaction blocker end-to-end, including the card reader's inventory-context requirement that a raw scripted SendMessage(FrobWorldEnd) could not satisfy.
nodes.norm_label: squirrel world-space frob scan + engine-frob publish-back -- confirmed working

nodes.label: ss2vr.ini Known-Keys Allowlist Silent-Rejection Bug
nodes.rationale: A second known-keys allowlist in Config.cpp (separate from the parser if/else chain) silently rejected new ini keys with 'Ignoring unknown ss2vr.ini key', voiding a whole test capture before anyone noticed. Lesson: any new ini key needs the parser branch, the allowlist entry, and the ini template edited together.
nodes.norm_label: ss2vr.ini known-keys allowlist silent-rejection bug

nodes.label: Hover-Candidate Bounding-Radius Size Cap + Filter Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: Discovered the native KEX frob picker scores hover candidates as distance-minus-bounding_radius with no upper bound, so large objects (doors/tables) always beat small interactables regardless of aim precision. world_candidate_max_radius rejects oversized candidates before the native scorer runs.
nodes.norm_label: hover-candidate bounding-radius size cap + filter diagnostic

nodes.label: VR View Effects System (GPU Post-Process: crt/aberration/lens/sharpen/glitch/edge)
nodes.rationale: Final 'keeper set' of 6 GPU scene-sampling post-process effects, driven by a D3D11 fullscreen pass at the CopyIntoSwapchain seam, with a reverse Squirrel->DLL trigger channel via the KexSetConfigRaw config-setter hook (set ss2vr_fx <effect>). That same config-setter hook was later found to collide with the unrelated weapon-pose bridge's own config-setter call, silently disabling weapon tracking.
nodes.norm_label: vr view effects system (gpu post-process: crt/aberration/lens/sharpen/glitch/edge)

nodes.label: VR Effects CPU-Overlay FPS Tank (root cause)
nodes.rationale: Creative overlay effects dropped framerate to ~10fps. Root cause: CPU-side regeneration of a 512^2 RGBA texture with per-pixel sin/cos/pow/exp every 90ms on the submit thread while the GPU sat idle. Fixed by moving to a GPU D3D11 fullscreen post-process pass instead of a CPU-regenerated overlay texture.
nodes.norm_label: vr effects cpu-overlay fps tank (root cause)

nodes.label: Native Dark Stereo-Enable Byte Probe (Dead End)
nodes.rationale: Tested whether the old pre-AE Dark engine stereo_enable/mirror_mode bytes could activate native side-by-side rendering in AE's D3D11 path. Console command and direct byte write both succeeded (readback confirmed) but produced no visible stereo output. Falsified as an activation route; parked in favor of the existing alternate-eye pair-lock baseline.
nodes.norm_label: native dark stereo-enable byte probe (dead end)

nodes.label: Weapon Viewmodel HMD Positional Parallax (double-applied HMD translation)
nodes.rationale: Moving the HMD with the controller held still made the weapon model slide away, as if HMD movement were doubled. Root cause: the pose bridge publishes controller-relative-to-head offset, then RenderView's own HMD 6DOF translation is applied again on top. Fixed with model_pose_compensate_hmd, which adds the HMD positional delta back into the CameraObj pose so it cancels the double application; projectile world origin stays on the raw physical pose so Stage A aim is unaffected.
nodes.norm_label: weapon viewmodel hmd positional parallax (double-applied hmd translation)

nodes.label: FunkMaxExport 3ds Max LGMD Tool Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Project-owned (non-GPL, built fresh rather than porting the Blender Dark exporter) 3ds Max <-> LGMD v4 bridge, built in tiers: exact no-edit round-trip, Funk Direct (topology-preserving vertex move), and Funk Mesh (vertex move + full-face deletion), enabling forearm removal from first-person weapon viewmodels while keeping AE's runtime PointRig/CameraObj animation working.
nodes.norm_label: funkmaxexport 3ds max lgmd tool pipeline

nodes.label: Funk Direct Baked-Import-Pose Bug
nodes.rationale: Funk Direct exported Max's displayed/world-space vertex positions for animated subobjects (the reload-hand and slide), baking the Max import pose into the LGMD file so the reload hand became permanently stuck onscreen. Fixed by choosing raw vs inverse-node-transform coordinates per subobject, compared against the original LGMD local vertices.
nodes.norm_label: funk direct baked-import-pose bug

nodes.label: Funk Mesh Stale Header Face-Count Crash
nodes.rationale: Funk Mesh compacted the LGMD face chunk after face deletion but left the header's face-count field at offset 0x3C unchanged, so AE walked past the compacted chunk using the old count and crashed with an access violation. Fixed by updating both the face count (0x3C) and vertex count (0x3E) header fields whenever chunks are rebuilt.
nodes.norm_label: funk mesh stale header face-count crash

nodes.label: Funk Mesh BSP Node-Offset Hang
nodes.rationale: After fixing the face-count crash, the same compacted export instead hung/froze AE with runaway render-record allocation. Root cause: face-chunk compaction changed BSP node record sizes, but only subobject node offsets were updated -- stale child-node offsets inside type-1 split and type-2 call node headers still pointed into the middle of the compacted stream, so AE's traversal generated millions of bogus render records.
nodes.norm_label: funk mesh bsp node-offset hang

nodes.label: FunkMesh modinfo.json Missing 'title' Key Crash
nodes.rationale: The repack step used the JSON key 'name' instead of AE's expected 'title' and omitted 'requirements':[]. AE is not defensive here: a missing title becomes a non-string JSON value and the mod-list UI crashes calling asCString() on it, before the already-fixed model even loads.
nodes.norm_label: funkmesh modinfo.json missing 'title' key crash

nodes.label: Right-Hand Aim Misdiagnosis: Sealed-Class Monkey-Patch of NDShootTriggerScript.OnCreate
nodes.rationale: WRONG APPROACH: direct assignment to NDShootTriggerScript.OnCreate is not legal in the AE Squirrel runtime/class context ('[SS2VR-AIM] projectile aim patch failed: trying to set class'). The failure was mistaken at first for a DLL pose-bridge or native-fire problem; the actual fix required a supported hook route (a parallel SqRootScript attached via the same ND.Archetype helper Nightdive itself uses).
nodes.norm_label: right-hand aim misdiagnosis: sealed-class monkey-patch of ndshoottriggerscript.oncreate

nodes.label: Right-Hand Aim Deferred-Timer Redirect Fix (v1.8, CONFIRMED)
nodes.rationale: The engine assigns a fired projectile's real launch velocity AFTER the script's OnCreate callback runs, so an immediate redirect always saw oldSpeed=0 and silently did nothing. Fix: re-apply the redirect from a SetOneShotTimer('SS2VRReaim', ...) deferred callback, which sees the real engine-assigned velocity (oldSpeed=300) and overwrites it along the controller ray while preserving speed.
nodes.norm_label: right-hand aim deferred-timer redirect fix (v1.8, confirmed)

nodes.label: Mod Load-Order/Priority Regression (KPF present but Squirrel not loaded)
nodes.rationale: Recurring failure mode: a KPF can appear in DarkDBMod's search paths and still fail to provide the active Squirrel load order if a higher-priority mod (e.g. sshock2ee) ships its own squirrel.ini first. The DLL side (pose bridge, native fire) can look fully alive while the Squirrel handler simply never loaded, producing a misleading 'regression' that looks like a code bug.
nodes.norm_label: mod load-order/priority regression (kpf present but squirrel not loaded)

nodes.label: KPF Archive Backslash-Path Packaging Bug
nodes.rationale: A repack step wrote archive entries with backslash paths (sq_scripts\squirrel.ini) instead of forward slashes, which likely prevented AE from recognizing/running the Squirrel load order even though the KPF was present in the mod search path -- another silent-looking Squirrel-not-loaded failure mode distinct from priority ordering.
nodes.norm_label: kpf archive backslash-path packaging bug

nodes.label: Save Patcher Default Insertion-Position Bug (first vs last)
nodes.rationale: The save patcher's add command defaulted to inserting the SS2VR mod entry FIRST in the saved game's mod table, which is the opposite of the desired effective load order (SS2VR needs to load after sshock2ee to win priority). Fixed by flipping the default --position to last.
nodes.norm_label: save patcher default insertion-position bug (first vs last)

nodes.label: Save Patcher Short-Root Save Shape Fix
nodes.rationale: A different/smaller save (smaller header_size/root object length/vtable length) failed the patcher's root-object shape guard even though the needed title/level/mods fields still parsed cleanly. Guard relaxed to accept shorter root objects as long as the specific required fields fit inside them.
nodes.norm_label: save patcher short-root save shape fix

nodes.label: FlatAim Native-Picker Diagonal Selection Offset
nodes.rationale: Even after 1:1-pixel visible-reticle-to-injected-picker logging proved no X/Y sign or overlay-placement error, the native KEX picker only selected objects when the visible reticle was aimed diagonally down-left of them. The user explicitly recognized this as the same shape as the VR mod's earlier frob 'offset diagonally'/tiny-sweet-spot problem; flat-pixel offset tuning was abandoned in favor of porting the SS2VR semantic world-space object scan + publish-back architecture to FlatAim.
nodes.norm_label: flataim native-picker diagonal selection offset

nodes.label: FlatAim Save-Load Access-Violation Crash (near native hover-candidate scorer)
nodes.rationale: Recurring access violation (0xc0000005) on loading/reloading a save while FlatAim was active, backtrace repeatedly landing near the hooked native hover-candidate scorer (0x1404B9EB6 / static RVA 0x8D4700-0x8D4748). Successive hypotheses (per-frame ss2fa_hl config mutation, missing Squirrel heartbeat, the installed KexSetConfigRaw hook itself) were each ruled out in turn -- disabling the config hook entirely (configHook=0 configInstalled=0) still did not stop the crash, leaving the true cause unresolved at the end of this range.
nodes.norm_label: flataim save-load access-violation crash (near native hover-candidate scorer)

nodes.label: Additive Left-Hand Viewmodel Spike (Phase 4.7)
nodes.rationale: Proof-of-concept second first-person viewmodel object cloned from the active weapon model, driven through the same Squirrel CameraObj property path proven by the right-hand handoff. Not true left-controller tracking yet: it follows the right hand's camera-local ss2vr_aim pose plus an offset because the left hand only publishes a world-space ss2vr_sel ray, not a camera-local pose.
nodes.norm_label: additive left-hand viewmodel spike (phase 4.7)

nodes.label: Weapon Pose Bridge Disabled by Own Config-Setter Hook Collision
nodes.rationale: User reported losing motion-controller weapon tracking after enabling an offhand-animation probe; root cause was unrelated and self-inflicted: the VR view-effects/config-trigger MinHook had detoured the same KEX config-setter function the weapon pose bridge used to publish ss2vr_aim, so the bridge's own prologue-mismatch safety check saw its own patched bytes and refused to publish. Fixed by routing through the g_realSetConfigRaw trampoline when the hook is installed.
nodes.norm_label: weapon pose bridge disabled by own config-setter hook collision

nodes.label: Weapon Model Rotational HMD Parallax (yaw/pitch/roll coupling)
nodes.rationale: After positional HMD-parallax compensation was fixed, a distinct rotational symptom remained: HMD yaw moves the pistol opposite, HMD pitch-down pushes the gun forward (and vice versa), and HMD roll rolls the pistol opposite. Addressed with a CameraObj-only rotational HMD compensation term layered after the existing positional compensation, plus a short pose latch/smoothing window; still jittery/unresolved at the end of this range.
nodes.norm_label: weapon model rotational hmd parallax (yaw/pitch/roll coupling)

nodes.label: Enemy Health Bar Misdiagnosis Correction: It Is Native
nodes.rationale: WRONG ASSUMPTION corrected: the team initially treated the enemy/target health bar as a build-from-scratch VR feature. A user screenshot proved AE already renders a native segmented HP bar in the flat 2D HUD layer. The real problem is VR placement/floating it above the world-space bracket, not implementing HP display from scratch.
nodes.norm_label: enemy health bar misdiagnosis correction: it is native

nodes.label: Native UI Draw-Range Index Slice Map (Phase 2.8)
nodes.rationale: Percentage-based and index-range captures of the native D3D11 UI draw calls, isolating which draw-index bands correspond to which coherent inventory/HUD element clusters (ammo/toggles, research/map buttons, inventory panel, weapon icons, MFD/keycard buttons, etc.), intended to replace percentage-slice UI panel placement with real draw-identity-based floating panels.
nodes.norm_label: native ui draw-range index slice map (phase 2.8)

nodes.label: Curved HUD/Inventory Panel Prototype
nodes.rationale: Cylindrical curvature applied to the floating inventory/HUD panel; low curvature felt small/far, high curvature (panel_curvature=0.95) felt close but the size-vs-distance scaling relationship still felt wrong, and curved mode disabled flat motion-controller inventory interaction as an expected side effect.
nodes.norm_label: curved hud/inventory panel prototype

nodes.label: FlatAim KPF Tar-Format Mount Failure
nodes.rationale: F5 was assumed blocked by hotkey/DLL/load-order problems; the KPF package was actually tar-format while working mods are ZIP/PK, so KEX could not mount kpf:/mods/flataim/ paths (path not found). Repacking as ZIP/PK fixed the Squirrel bridge load.
nodes.norm_label: flataim kpf tar-format mount failure

nodes.label: FlatAim KexSetConfigRaw Hook Crash Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Wrong theory: the installed KexSetConfigRaw config-setter detour was suspected as the cause of a save-load crash at RVA 0x8D4700. Disabling the hook entirely (config_hook=0, then block_without_bridge=1) did not stop the crash, falsifying the config hook as direct cause.
nodes.norm_label: flataim kexsetconfigraw hook crash misdiagnosis

nodes.label: Contaminated Debug-View Save Crash Root Cause
nodes.rationale: Root cause found after the config-hook theory was falsified: the crashing 'Flataim' save was created during an earlier FlatAim build while debug_view_enabled was active, persisting bad debug-view/cursor-mode/list state. A fresh save created after leaving debug view loaded successfully, confirming the old save was a contaminated-state artifact rather than a live bug.
nodes.norm_label: contaminated debug-view save crash root cause

nodes.label: Native Cursor Globals Crosshair-Driver Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Wrong theory: writing the FlatAim internal cursor pixel into KEX native cursor globals DAT_1413179b8/938 was expected to move the visible stock crosshair. Readback moved but the visible crosshair stayed centered, falsifying the native cursor globals as the crosshair's actual driver; work pivoted to a ShockOverlay-drawn replacement reticle (kOverlayCrosshair=22).
nodes.norm_label: native cursor globals crosshair-driver misdiagnosis

nodes.label: ShockOverlay Reticle Origin-Bias Fix
nodes.rationale: The replacement ShockOverlay reticle appeared offset right/down from the DLL-published center aim. Root cause was a ShockOverlay draw-origin/safe-area bias; v0.9 fixed it by subtracting hudCanvas/16 (about 60x33.75 HUD px) before DrawBitmap.
nodes.norm_label: shockoverlay reticle origin-bias fix

nodes.label: FlatAim Stale Startup Aim Clear Fix
nodes.rationale: After the origin-bias fix, the normal gameplay crosshair appeared offset on load before F5 was even pressed. Root cause: stale valid ss2fa_aim state survived from a previous run into script load/startup. Fixed by clearing ss2fa_aim on script load and publishing an invalid startup aim from the DLL.
nodes.norm_label: flataim stale startup aim clear fix

nodes.label: FlatAim Visible Weapon Pitch-Dependent Roll Bug
nodes.rationale: Recurring symptom across a dozen-plus builds (v0.11-v0.28): horizontal mouse aim visually turns into weapon roll as camera pitch rises, with roll direction flipping above/below horizon. Root cause was ultimately a heading-axis-convention mismatch, not a sign/offset problem.
nodes.norm_label: flataim visible weapon pitch-dependent roll bug

nodes.label: CameraObj Euler Scalar Roll-Compensation Misdiagnosis (Modes 1-6)
nodes.rationale: Wrong theory pursued across weapon_follow_mode 1 through 6: that scalar Heading/Pitch/Bank formula tuning and sign flips on the final native CameraObj representation could fix the pitch-dependent roll. Every variant (cos/sin compensation, bank cancellation, rig-level aimPoint insertion, screen-axis variants) was falsified by live retest; the user explicitly challenged whether the team understood the issue or was 'layering band-aids.'
nodes.norm_label: cameraobj euler scalar roll-compensation misdiagnosis (modes 1-6)

nodes.label: FlatAim World-Space Weapon Proxy (Mode 7)
nodes.rationale: After scalar CameraObj tuning was abandoned, v0.20 introduced a transient world-space object cloned from the weapon model, hidden the native viewmodel, and positioned/faced independently via Object.Teleport. Multiple facing-decomposition sub-attempts (facingMode 0/1/4/5/6/7) still rolled until the true Dark heading convention was found.
nodes.norm_label: flataim world-space weapon proxy (mode 7)

nodes.label: Dark Heading-Axis Convention Root Cause Fix
nodes.rationale: Root cause: Dark's matrix inverse reads world-object heading as atan2(forward.y, forward.x), while FlatAim's proxy heading computation used atan2(dir.x, dir.y) -- a swapped-argument convention mismatch, not a sign or scalar-tuning problem. Mode 8 rebuilt an upright Dark basis (forward/right/up) and extracted heading/pitch/bank using the correct atan2 argument order.
nodes.norm_label: dark heading-axis convention root cause fix

nodes.label: FlatAim Ray-Cylinder Object Selector Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Wrong approach: the original selector scored candidate objects by origin-distance to a 3D ray cylinder, so clustered floor pistols with similar origin-to-ray distances could hop or win selection from surprising screen positions, unlike inventory-mode cursor picking.
nodes.norm_label: flataim ray-cylinder object selector misdiagnosis

nodes.label: FlatAim Screen-Projected Semantic Selection (Mode 2)
nodes.rationale: Fix for the ray-cylinder misdiagnosis: selection_semantic_mode=2 projects candidate objects with ShockOverlay.WorldToScreen and compares them to the actual drawn reticle point, matching inventory-style cursor picking. User confirmed it 'solved the selection issue in one pass.'
nodes.norm_label: flataim screen-projected semantic selection (mode 2)

nodes.label: FlatAim Native-Looking Bracket Marker (BRACK0-3)
nodes.rationale: Draws stock BRACK0-3 ShockOverlay bitmaps around the screen-projected semantic target as a substitute for the still-uninvestigated true native bracket path; user reported the visuals were 'WAY better.'
nodes.norm_label: flataim native-looking bracket marker (brack0-3)

nodes.label: FlatAim Laser Bolt Rotation Reflection Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: First patch attempt treated the rotated (horizontal blue line) Laser Pistol bolt as a reflection-style visual-orientation bug and was wrong. The actual cause was the same heading-axis-convention issue as the weapon roll bug: FlatAim aim heading used atan2(x,y) from +Y while KEX object facing needed atan2(y,x) from +X.
nodes.norm_label: flataim laser bolt rotation reflection misdiagnosis

nodes.label: FlatAim Long-Weapon Proxy Pivot Fix
nodes.rationale: Long weapons rotated around the short-gun/pistol origin so their butt swung into view at low-right aim. Fixed as a proxy pivot/model-origin placement problem (weapon_proxy_pivot_long_forward/left/up), explicitly not a reticle/projectile/facing math fix.
nodes.norm_label: flataim long-weapon proxy pivot fix

nodes.label: FlatAim Melee Viewmodel Spin/Orbit Bug
nodes.rationale: Root cause: native NDShockMeleeViewmodel.OnFrameUpdate() only writes PlyrArm Location, never Heading/Pitch/Bank; FlatAim's orientation writes to those fields were therefore fighting/compounding with native state and caused the Wrench to spin rapidly around the player on left/right aim. Fixed by making mode 3 write no facing fields (writeFacing=0) and using camera-screen-plane location offset only.
nodes.norm_label: flataim melee viewmodel spin/orbit bug

nodes.label: FlatAim F5 Blocked by Squirrel Syntax Error
nodes.rationale: F5 doing nothing looked like the recurring Squirrel-bridge-missing symptom, but condump.txt showed the real cause was a Squirrel compile error (extra closing parenthesis in an [SS2FA-MELEE] pose diagnostic print) that prevented ss2fa.nut from loading at all.
nodes.norm_label: flataim f5 blocked by squirrel syntax error

nodes.label: Viewmodel World-Depth Occlusion Spike (Phase 4.2.2)
nodes.rationale: D3D11 hook remembers non-backbuffer scene color/depth at draw time, arms on a pointer-matched depth clear, then preserves/binds that depth around the viewmodel DrawIndexed cluster so nearby world geometry occludes the weapon. Confirmed live in headset: 'YES! Depth occlusion is WORKING!!' Kept default-off pending a broader multi-weapon regression sweep.
nodes.norm_label: viewmodel world-depth occlusion spike (phase 4.2.2)

nodes.label: Existing-Save Patcher Root-Object Shape Fix
nodes.rationale: The offline save patcher's root-object guard rejected a smaller/different save (header_size=0xF8, root length 0x24) with 'unexpected root table/vtable shape' even though the needed title/level/mods fields existed. Relaxed the guard to accept shorter root objects when those specific fields exist and fit.
nodes.norm_label: existing-save patcher root-object shape fix

nodes.label: Left-Hand Additive Viewmodel Shaded-Material White/Purple Bug
nodes.rationale: Long A/B probe saga: the additive standalone left-hand model rendered bright self-illuminated white (or purple/black with a red-material probe) under every shaded material variant tried (custom opaque material, copied ND-arm.dds, $TEXTURE, explicit local paths), while the same texture/mesh rendered correctly under an unshaded (shaded 0) pass. Isolated the bug to the shaded/lit render path specifically, not texture lookup or model geometry.
nodes.norm_label: left-hand additive viewmodel shaded-material white/purple bug

nodes.label: Left-Hand Material Include-Chain Packaging Root Cause
nodes.rationale: Root cause: the custom package .mtl included ../../materials/ND-hand.inc, but that include chain was never packaged inside the SS2VR KPF. Stock ND-arm.mtl resolves its ../../materials/ND-viewmodel.inc include from the base sshock2ee package, but custom package-local materials resolve relative to their own KPF and crash/fail when the include is missing. Fixed in KPF v1.49 by packaging ND-pass_dif/fill/rim.inc and ND-IR_rim.png locally.
nodes.norm_label: left-hand material include-chain packaging root cause

nodes.label: Jointed Standalone LGMD Root-Subobject Crash
nodes.rationale: Preserving source joint metadata (motion_type=2,joint_id=2) on a one-subobject standalone hand extract crashed AE with a null-pointer access violation at .text:1408F8B6B, because in the known-good model that subobject is a jointed child in a full hierarchy, not a root. Falsified 'preserve source joint metadata' for standalone single-subobject extracts; the exporter now rejects that combination. Static-metadata rebuild alone still crashed until the include-chain root cause was also fixed.
nodes.norm_label: jointed standalone lgmd root-subobject crash

nodes.label: RenderDoc Stock Blue Viewmodel Invis-Pass Finding
nodes.rationale: RenderDoc capture showed every stock viewmodel (pistol, right hand, left hand) is first drawn as transparent blue via ND-pass_invis.inc before its normal pass. Correction to an earlier assumption: a bad additive left hand looking blue is not material-ID corruption, it means the later normal/lit/fill/rim pass is missing, failing, or being dominated by this intentional first pass.
nodes.norm_label: renderdoc stock blue viewmodel invis-pass finding

nodes.label: FunkMaxExport v0.6.0-customgroup Build
nodes.rationale: Added general build_custom_lgmd_bytes() core writer supporting multi-subobject mesh-group export with child/sibling hierarchy, named vhot_## helper export, rebuilt material tables, and a Package KPF button. LGMM/.CAL skeleton/weights and rotating PointRig joint authoring remained deferred; runtime AE proof was still pending at build time.
nodes.norm_label: funkmaxexport v0.6.0-customgroup build

nodes.label: Native UI Draw-Range Scanner
nodes.rationale: Opt-in [ / ] hotkeys step individual native UI draw candidates. Proved the draw-number-to-panel mapping is not a fixed semantic ID list -- draw numbers shift by gameplay/inventory mode and equipped/carried items -- so final panel extraction must group by destination rect/bound texture/overlay slot, not draw ordinal.
nodes.norm_label: native ui draw-range scanner

nodes.label: Native Overlay Rect Rearrange Spike (Phase 2.8.1)
nodes.rationale: Spike rewrites gOverlayRects[50] to rearrange the 2D HUD (swap top/bottom bands) after validating the gOverlayOrder[50] signature. First pass captured the rect table too early and wrote from zero rects, collapsing icons to top-left; fixed by waiting for usable anchor rects (kOverlayInv/Ammo/Meters) before capture, then generalized to transform every usable rect by vertical band instead of a few named panels.
nodes.norm_label: native overlay rect rearrange spike (phase 2.8.1)

nodes.label: Right-Arm HUD Native-Rect Source Fix
nodes.rationale: The percentage-crop 'slice' method for the right-arm ammo hologram broke when inventory opened because the flat HUD graphic expanded and pulled in unrelated lower-right inventory/MFD data. Replaced with a native_rect mode that reads the validated gOverlayRects[50] ammo rect directly and fails closed (signature_mismatch/overlay_inactive/rect_invalid) instead of silently falling back to the known-bad slice.
nodes.norm_label: right-arm hud native-rect source fix

nodes.label: SS2VR Triple Selection-Bracket System Confusion
nodes.rationale: Initially treated as one 'doubled bracket' bug. User correction clarified it was actually three separate systems: (1) unwanted SS2VR deep-world bracket on large non-interactable objects via a stale KEX objectUnderCursor fallback, (2) wanted SS2VR deep-world bracket on Squirrel-selected frobbable objects, and (3) the native flat 2D HUD bracket, misaligned in VR. Fixing (1) alone (dropping the objectUnderCursor fallback) then surfaced Squirrel highlight pollution (ss2vr_hl flicker) as the next-layer bug, stabilized with a hover latch.
nodes.norm_label: ss2vr triple selection-bracket system confusion

nodes.label: SS2VR Selection Bracket Stereo-Eye Convergence Fix
nodes.rationale: Root cause of a remaining lagging duplicate bracket copy: the shared both-eyes bracket marker was computed from the post-stereo per-eye newView, so alternating eye offsets polluted a marker meant to be mono/stable. Fixed by computing the marker against the pre-eye-offset mono view (flatResidualView), falling back to newView only if unavailable.
nodes.norm_label: ss2vr selection bracket stereo-eye convergence fix

nodes.label: Native Crosshair/Center-Frob Suppression
nodes.rationale: Adds suppress_native_crosshair/center_frob/brackets with a tracking-loss grace window: while controllers track, hides native overlay 22 and clears native object-under-cursor/hover/frob globals so objects can only be interacted with via controllers; falls back to native centre-crosshair frobbing if controller tracking is lost.
nodes.norm_label: native crosshair/center-frob suppression

nodes.label: SS2VR Weapon Viewmodel HMD-Bleed Recurring Failure
nodes.rationale: Recurring failure mode across many builds (Phase 4.2.1, retested through v1.41-v1.43): the visible right-hand weapon model keeps reacting to HMD position/rotation instead of staying locked to the motion controller, despite projectile/world aim (pose_diag_right w*/dir fields) staying stable throughout. Roll-only compensation, disabling HMD rotational/positional compensation flags, and CameraObj translation remaps each reduced but did not fully eliminate the symptom; isolated to AE's CameraObj viewmodel-consumption path rather than the OpenXR pose bridge.
nodes.norm_label: ss2vr weapon viewmodel hmd-bleed recurring failure

nodes.label: Headset UI Invisibility Fix (Force UI Quad Submission)
nodes.rationale: Inventory, gameplay HUD, and the main menu were invisible in headset (visible only on the desktop mirror) after enabling the right-arm HUD hologram path, because D3D only supplied a UI texture to OpenXR when submit_quad_layer, hand panel, or right-arm HUD were individually enabled. Fixed by passing uiFrameActive into OpenXR and always supplying the captured lastCandidateUiTexture_ so the full UI layer submits even with submit_quad_layer=false.
nodes.norm_label: headset ui invisibility fix (force ui quad submission)

nodes.label: Gravity-Glove Held-Object Facing Axis-Order Fix
nodes.rationale: Grabbed/held objects moved correctly but their rotation did not match controller rotation, with pitch/bank feeling switched. Iterated through hold-facing modes (4, then 5) and heading/pitch sign knobs (ss2vr_phys_hold_heading_sign=-1) to align the applied Dark object-order (bank,pitch,heading) facing with controller orientation.
nodes.norm_label: gravity-glove held-object facing axis-order fix

nodes.label: Snap-Turn Pixel-Per-Degree Gain Calibration
nodes.rationale: snap_turn_degrees=50 required about five right snaps to rotate 90 degrees, proving the pixel gain was under-rotating; a captured snap showed the route was effectively 1 pixel per degree while the config used snapPxPerDeg=1.40. Corrected the v1.49 default to snap_turn_pixels_per_degree=1.0 to match the observed KEX yaw-delta response.
nodes.norm_label: snap-turn pixel-per-degree gain calibration

nodes.label: Damage-Triggered Glitch FX Watcher
nodes.rationale: SS2VR.EffectHandler polls player HitPoints and on a drop sends a Debug.Command config trigger (ss2vr_fx glitch:<intensity>:<speed>) through the existing DLL config-setter hook/effect manager, reusing that hook as the only rendering path rather than adding a second FX system or native damage hook.
nodes.norm_label: damage-triggered glitch fx watcher

nodes.label: FlatAim Laser Bolt Facing-Axis Fix
nodes.rationale: First reflection-style patch for the visible-projectile rotation was wrong; the actual bug was a heading-axis convention mismatch: FlatAim aim heading uses atan2(x,y) from +Y while KEX object facing needs atan2(y,x) from +X. Fixed via SS2FA_DirToProjectileObjectFacing().
nodes.norm_label: flataim laser bolt facing-axis fix

nodes.label: FlatAim Wrench/Melee Viewmodel Implementation
nodes.rationale: Added SS2FAMeleeViewmodel extends NDShockMeleeViewmodel to retarget PlyrArm from FlatAim view-frame aim after native melee update runs, letting Wrench and other melee weapons track the FlatAim crosshair.
nodes.norm_label: flataim wrench/melee viewmodel implementation

nodes.label: FlatAim Melee Orientation-Mode Investigation
nodes.rationale: Multi-step debugging arc for melee aim-follow: direct proxy-facing writes to PlyrArm (mode 2) made the Wrench disappear on F5; native-relative heading/bank writes caused rapid spin/orbit; the eventual mode 3 fix writes no PlyrArm facing at all and follows the reticle via camera-screen-plane location offset only, using point-rig local-frame axes (X=forward, Y=left, Z=up) rather than gun-proxy axes.
nodes.norm_label: flataim melee orientation-mode investigation

nodes.label: FlatAim Pickup Reach Regression
nodes.rationale: FreeAim pickup range appeared extended versus stock; root cause was a stale selection_semantic_reach=20.0 override in flataim.ini left over from earlier selection tuning, while the compiled fallback and stock frob reach were both 8 KEX units.
nodes.norm_label: flataim pickup reach regression

nodes.label: FlatAim Ultrawide Overlay-Canvas Coordinate Bug
nodes.rationale: At 3440x1440 the crosshair started off-center. Root cause: Squirrel ShockOverlay code used Engine.GetCanvasSize()/2, correct only at 1920x1080 where it happens to equal the fixed 960x540 overlay canvas. Two more iterations were needed: a fixed-960x540 fix still snapped left until a hidden native HUD-origin bias was disabled; final fix treats ShockOverlay as height-normalized (hudY=540, hudX=rawW*540/rawH).
nodes.norm_label: flataim ultrawide overlay-canvas coordinate bug

nodes.label: FlatAim Dynamic Canvas Sizing
nodes.rationale: Initial Freelook crosshair position behaved as if 1920x1080 was baked in at other resolutions. Fixed by publishing the live KEX canvas size (ss2fa_canvas) from Engine.GetCanvasSize() through the config bridge, which in turn exposed the separate overlay-canvas coordinate-space bug.
nodes.norm_label: flataim dynamic canvas sizing

nodes.label: FlatAim Edge-Pan View Follow
nodes.rationale: Adds view movement as the freeaim cursor nears the screen edge; writes synthetic native yaw/pitch accumulators and calls native PlayerTurnTilt when the reticle enters an edge band, ramped by proximity to the edge.
nodes.norm_label: flataim edge-pan view follow

nodes.label: Left-Hand Additive Model Material-Invisibility Investigation
nodes.rationale: Investigation of why candidate left-hand models (ss2vr_lk, ss2vr_lj, ss2vr_lm, ss2vr_ln) failed to render visibly despite reaching the additive viewmodel render path. ss2vr_lk rendered but contributed no visible pixels (lit-stack problem); ss2vr_lm was invisible; ss2vr_ln crashed AE. A compact-vs-five-slot material-table A/B found no safe lit path, so the known-visible flatlit ss2vr_ls fallback was restored as default, with lj/lk/lm/ln parked behind a redirect guard pending a RenderDoc A/B against the stock hand.
nodes.norm_label: left-hand additive model material-invisibility investigation

nodes.label: Left-Hand Pose-Loss Hide Confound
nodes.rationale: Early left-hand material tests were confounded by ss2vr_lhand_hide_on_pose_loss=1 destroying/hiding the additive hand before creation whenever the left controller pose was invalid, masking whether the underlying material/BIN was the real problem.
nodes.norm_label: left-hand pose-loss hide confound

nodes.label: Vanilla Gamepad Analog Injector Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY pursued initially: physical-controller analog movement/view failure in vanilla SS2:AE (without the SS2VR injector) was suspected to be a KEX cvar/injector-path problem, prompting an experimental native_axis_direct workaround. ROOT CAUSE actually found: a stale joystick_enable 0 line in user.bnd, synced and persisted across reinstalls/PCs by Steam Cloud, disabled the legacy joystick axis consumer. Fixing that line restored physical-controller analog input in vanilla AE with no injector change needed.
nodes.norm_label: vanilla gamepad analog injector misdiagnosis

nodes.label: SS2VR native_axis_direct Experimental Input Path

nodes.label: LGMD/LGMM/LGPMNM Mesh Format Family
nodes.rationale: LGMD is the static/animated viewmodel mesh format used by gun and static weapon carriers. LGMM is a separate skeletal/AI mesh format (needs companion .CAL joint data) used by melee arm rigs like pipewrench_h.bin/wrench_h.bin; direct LGMM export is not implemented, so LGMM sources are converted through FreeTheObjects into referenceable geometry instead. LGPMNM is a high-detail mesh payload embedded inside some LGMM/LGMD files.
nodes.norm_label: lgmd/lgmm/lgpmnm mesh format family

nodes.label: LGPMNM Embedded High-Detail Mesh Discovery
nodes.rationale: Discovered that pipewrench_h.bin and wrench_h.bin embed a high-detail LGPMNM payload after the classic low-poly LGMM core (materials ND-melee_arm.psd plus wrench-specific slots), explaining why FunkMax's classic LGMM importer only ever produced the low-poly arm. The same payload family (short PMNM-wrapper form, missing the LG prefix) was later found in rapier_h.bin, psword_h.bin, and shard_h.bin.
nodes.norm_label: lgpmnm embedded high-detail mesh discovery

nodes.label: Animated Hand-Husk Crash Investigation
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage misdiagnosis arc for weapon-equip crashes after hand-removal trims. Stage 1 (WRONG): zero-face animated hand subobjects (@s01_han etc.) were assumed safe if parse-clean; a safe-stub exporter converted them to one-face hidden stubs. Stage 2 (falsified): one-face husks still crashed on weapon-switch in headset even though mouse-wheel switching outside VR looked fine; the validator was extended to block near-empty (<=1 face) animated hand/han subobjects and pistol/AR/laser overrides were pulled back to stock fallback. Stage 3 (resolution): specific one-face hand-stub BINs were live-proven per weapon and allowlisted by exact SHA256 rather than by a general structural rule.
nodes.norm_label: animated hand-husk crash investigation

nodes.label: Stale LGMD Light/Normal Aux-Range Bug
nodes.rationale: After face deletion, source-preserving LGMD exports (shotgun, EMP) kept the original stale subobject light/normal record ranges even though far fewer records were actually referenced by the remaining faces, unlike stock LGMDs which have exact contiguous ranges. Fixed by an auxcompact pass that compacts lights/normals together with faces/nodes.
nodes.norm_label: stale lgmd light/normal aux-range bug

nodes.label: Stale LGMD v4 Material-Extras/Tail Bug
nodes.rationale: The earlier fix of zeroing v4 material-extra header fields on source-preserving exports was itself wrong: vanilla LGMDs keep populated material-extra fields (material_offset + 26*num_materials pattern) and a correct v4 end offset. Zeroing them mismatched the still-present aux material bytes and left a stale end-offset pointing at the original larger stock file size. Fixed by repairing/repointing extras and the end offset instead of zeroing, with the validator extended to fail zeroed/stale v4 tails.
nodes.norm_label: stale lgmd v4 material-extras/tail bug

nodes.label: Custom .mtl Include-Chain Crash
nodes.rationale: Packaging custom .mtl sidecars with include statements (e.g. ../../materials/ND-viewmodel.inc) caused a null-read AV crash on save-load, matching an earlier pattern seen with ss2vr_lj. Fixed by rewriting the .mtl files as fully inline material scripts with no include lines.
nodes.norm_label: custom .mtl include-chain crash

nodes.label: AR15 Custom-Vhot Loader Crash Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: adding custom high-ID vhots (80/81/82) to the live-good AR15 crashed KEX's native LGMD loader before menu, first attributed to high/non-contiguous vhot IDs; remapping to low IDs (2/3/4) still crashed identically, falsifying that theory. ROOT CAUSE (Ghidra plus stock comparison): LGMD header byte 68 (num_vhots) was stale, left at 2 even though 5 vhot records were written; stock sg_h.bin's byte 68=3 matches its 3 vhots. Fixed by rewriting header bytes 66..69 during rebuild and adding a validator check for stale header counts.
nodes.norm_label: ar15 custom-vhot loader crash misdiagnosis

nodes.label: Stale LGMD Header Count Confound (ss2vr_wrench_h)
nodes.rationale: After the byte-68 AR15 fix, a retest still crashed, but crash-dump/KPF forensics showed the installed package did not even contain the patched AR15 - the real active suspect was a stale header vhot/subobject count on an unrelated static viewmodel (ss2vr_wrench_h, byte 69 num_subobjects stale) entering the same native vhot-builder path. Repairing header counts on all custom ss2vr_* static assets, not just the AR15, let the save load and proved the AR15 vhot fix was viable all along.
nodes.norm_label: stale lgmd header count confound (ss2vr_wrench_h)

nodes.label: Weapon-Equip INT3 Crash: Zero-Face Animated Subobjects
nodes.rationale: Root-caused via crashlog (BREAKPOINT at SystemShock2Remastered.exe+0x94EBCB, in-memory LGMD name Grip00C) to the pistol viewmodel override obj/atek_h.bin retaining two animated zero-face hand subobjects (@s01_han, @s02_han); the same pattern existed in parked ss2vr_assault_rifle.bin and ss2vr_lasehand.bin. Fixed short-term by removing the risky stock-name overrides and gating any future model swap behind an explicit unsafe flag, plus a new validate_lgmd_runtime_safety.py check.
nodes.norm_label: weapon-equip int3 crash: zero-face animated subobjects

nodes.label: One-Face Hand-Stub Live-Proof Ladder
nodes.rationale: Per-weapon incremental live-testing strategy after the general one-face-stub theory was falsified: test pistol alone (v1.90, accepted SHA 33AF51F8...), then AR15 alone (v1.91, live-good), then laser pistol alone (v1.92, live-good), each promoted to the validator's exact-SHA allowlist only after headset-confirmed stability, rather than trusting a general structural rule.
nodes.norm_label: one-face hand-stub live-proof ladder

nodes.label: Static Wrench LGPMNM Export Visual-Fix Saga
nodes.rationale: Iterative visual-correctness pass on the LGPMNM-derived static wrench+hand carrier (ss2vr_wrench_h.bin) after it first rendered but looked too small, rotated, dark, and faceted: principal-length check showed apparent half-size was a carrier scale/pivot illusion, not literal geometry scaling; smoothing-group-aware packed light-normal generation fixed faceted shading; LGPMNM material alpha/emission metadata preservation fixed lost self-illumination on ND-wrench_il.psd; a final packed light-normal inversion (rolled into v0.6.30-lgpmnmlightfix) fixed lighting appearing on the wrong side of the mesh.
nodes.norm_label: static wrench lgpmnm export visual-fix saga

nodes.label: Shotgun Animated-Pump Vhot Crash
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: adding vhots to the shotgun caused an equip crash, initially treated as evidence that extra vhots were unsafe on this weapon even though the exported BIN passed strict structural validation. ROOT CAUSE: the vhot export had gone through LGMD Custom instead of LGMD Modify Existing, which renamed/reshaped the animated pump subobject (@00sli.0 -> @00sli_0, vertex range and face count changed); AE's Hybrid_Shotgun animations drive JointPos Joint 1 on that exact subobject identity/range, so altering it broke the animated pump binding. Fixed by re-exporting as a true vhot-only edit over the live-good base via LGMD Modify Existing, preserving the stock subobject name and vertex ranges exactly.
nodes.norm_label: shotgun animated-pump vhot crash

nodes.label: Weapon-Mesh Hand-Removal Trim Package

This trim work is what first exposed the animated-hand-husk crash class.

nodes.label: VR Grip/Reload Vhot Authoring Workflow
nodes.rationale: Tooling and convention for authoring motion-controller pivot/grip/reload markers directly in weapon LGMDs: adopted high-ID convention (80=pivot, 81=support grip, 82=reload) which later had to be remapped to low IDs after the header-count crash was found; required several FunkMax fixes for duplicate hidden vhot-id properties on cloned helpers, preserving accepted one-face hand stubs during vhot-only re-exports, skipping near-zero float-roundoff vertex deltas so metadata-only edits stay recognized as such, and baking LGPMNM static vhots in world/snapshot space so exported positions match the Max scene.
nodes.norm_label: vr grip/reload vhot authoring workflow

nodes.label: Decision: Permit Vhot-Only Edits to Carry Live-Good One-Face Stubs
nodes.rationale: LGMD Modify Existing may carry a live-proven one-face hand stub forward for vhot-only metadata edits so AR15 vhot authoring doesn't require rebuilding the ladder candidate or enabling the risky one-face-stub test checkbox. Superseded same-day by visible-name override fix.
nodes.norm_label: decision: permit vhot-only edits to carry live-good one-face stubs

nodes.label: Decision: Visible Vhot Helper Names Override Stale Cloned IDs
nodes.rationale: When a 3ds Max helper's visible vhot_## name disagrees with its hidden ss2vr_lgmd_vhot_id property (from cloning), the visible name wins, since artists expect renamed helpers to be authoritative. Fixed a duplicate-vhot-id-0 export failure. Superseded by v0.6.23-vhotcarry.
nodes.norm_label: decision: visible vhot helper names override stale cloned ids

nodes.label: Decision: Carry Accepted One-Face Source Stubs for Metadata-Only Edits
nodes.rationale: For live-proven vhot-free fingerprints (pistol/AR15/laser), preserve the source one-face hand stub during metadata edits even if the matching Max mesh/helper is missing, so losing a tiny visible stub doesn't force a risky new ladder export.
nodes.norm_label: decision: carry accepted one-face source stubs for metadata-only edits

nodes.label: Decision: Skip Sub-Epsilon Vertex Writes in Metadata-Only Exports
nodes.rationale: LGMD Modify Existing writes vertex positions only when the Max/source delta exceeds 1e-5, because sub-epsilon float round-trip noise changed the vhot-free fingerprint and made the strict validator treat metadata-only exports as unproven geometry variants.
nodes.norm_label: decision: skip sub-epsilon vertex writes in metadata-only exports

nodes.label: Decision: Accept Repaired One-Face Hand-Stub Overrides by Exact Digest
nodes.rationale: Accept the repaired one-face hand-stub pattern only for exact live-proven digests (atek_h.bin, ar15_h.bin, lasehand.bin); full pruning crashed and zero-face husks crashed/hung, so digest-specific allowlisting is the safe middle ground. Rejected: generic one-face-stub acceptance without live proof.
nodes.norm_label: decision: accept repaired one-face hand-stub overrides by exact digest

nodes.label: Decision (Falsified): Full Hand-Subobject Pruning for Pistol/AR/Laser
nodes.rationale: Tried removing deleted hand subobjects entirely and remapping BSP nodes as the next-smallest test after one-face stubs proved unsafe. Live testing falsified this: pistol/AR/laser still crashed, with AR's crash dump containing LGMD/ar15gun in the game-side loader. Superseded by v1.87 stock-rig rollback.
nodes.norm_label: decision (falsified): full hand-subobject pruning for pistol/ar/laser

nodes.label: Decision: Repair LGMD v4 Material Tails Instead of Zeroing Them
nodes.rationale: Zeroing (mat_flags, off_mat_extra, size_mat_extra) avoided stale donor pointers but the SG/EMP crash comparison showed the zeroed header itself was an equip-loader hazard. Exporters must repoint the v4 material-extra header to the current aux table and update the v4 end offset after compaction; validator rejects stale/zeroed extras for aux-bearing LGMDs.
nodes.norm_label: decision: repair lgmd v4 material tails instead of zeroing them

nodes.label: Decision: Treat Stale LGMD Light/Normal Ranges as Unsafe
nodes.rationale: EMP and shotgun still crashed/hung after hand-husk files were removed because face deletion left stale subobject light_offset/light_count and normal_offset/normal_count ranges. LGMD Modify Existing must compact light/normal chunks together with face/node chunks; validator must reject stale aux ranges.
nodes.norm_label: decision: treat stale lgmd light/normal ranges as unsafe

nodes.label: Decision: Treat One-Face Animated Hand Husks as Unsafe
nodes.rationale: The validator only rejected zero-face subobjects, so one-face stubbed exports (v0.6.12-safestubs) passed but still crashed/hung VR weapon switching. Extended the runtime-safety rule to also block one-retained-face hand children until live-proven otherwise.
nodes.norm_label: decision: treat one-face animated hand husks as unsafe

nodes.label: Decision: Park Runtime Weapon Swaps and Zero-Face Weapon Overrides
nodes.rationale: A game-side LGMD loader crash (INT3) traced to a same-name pistol override retaining zero-face animated hand subobjects, even though material extras were zeroed. Legacy ss2vr_weapon_model_swap must not enable runtime ModelName changes; runtime swaps require explicit unsafe opt-in plus strict validator pass.
nodes.norm_label: decision: park runtime weapon swaps and zero-face weapon overrides

nodes.label: Decision: Funk Mesh Missing Non-Root Nodes = Face Deletion, Not Subobject Removal
nodes.rationale: A missing imported non-root subobject mesh node in Max means 'delete all original faces from this preserved subobject,' keeping LGMD subobject/joint/node identity intact so AE weapon animation/PointRig can still reference it even with an empty face list. Funk Direct stays strict and move-only.
nodes.norm_label: decision: funk mesh missing non-root nodes = face deletion, not subobject removal

nodes.label: Decision: Keep LGMM Import Separate from LGMD Export
nodes.rationale: LGMM is a segmented/skinned mesh format paired with .CAL, while FunkMaxExport writers emit static LGMD; added read-only LGMM parsing/import tagged separately and excluded from LGMD export to avoid producing misleading assets. CAL/bind-pose/weights export not claimed until understood.
nodes.norm_label: decision: keep lgmm import separate from lgmd export

nodes.label: Decision: Restore Flatlit Left-Hand Baseline; RenderDoc Gates Further Material Work
nodes.rationale: ss2vr_ls (flatlit, shaded 0) is the only known-visible standalone custom hand fallback after ss2vr_lk/lm proved invisible and ss2vr_ln crashed; no new material variants before a RenderDoc A/B of the shaded-1 white state versus stock hand identifies the missing pass input.
nodes.norm_label: decision: restore flatlit left-hand baseline; renderdoc gates further material work

nodes.label: Decision: FlatAim Reticle Offset Moves to Native Overlay-Table Proof
nodes.rationale: Stop tuning Squirrel reticle offsets after the WorldToScreen aim-ray path was falsified as facing-dependent; use a read-only DLL probe of native overlay slot 22 (gOverlayOrder/gOverlayRects) to find the native rect/anchor first.
nodes.norm_label: decision: flataim reticle offset moves to native overlay-table proof

nodes.label: Decision: Treat Additive-Hand Render Proof and Visible Pixels as Separate Gates
nodes.rationale: Squirrel logging renderedThisFrame=1 is not proof of visible geometry; ss2vr_lk was selected/posed/reported rendered but the user still saw no mesh, so further probes must split GPU/visual contribution from BIN material-table shape and material pass behavior.
nodes.norm_label: decision: treat additive-hand render proof and visible pixels as separate gates

nodes.label: Decision: Aim/Facing Conventions Single-Sourced; SS2VR Brought to Parity with FlatAim
nodes.rationale: Shared Dark-engine aim/facing math is canonicalized in docs/CONVENTIONS.md; SS2VR and FlatAim stay separate products sharing conventions, not code. A graphify drift audit found SS2VR lacked engine-side heading/basis helpers FlatAim already had, causing inline math that produced the FlatAim laser-diagonal bug class.
nodes.norm_label: decision: aim/facing conventions single-sourced; ss2vr brought to parity with flataim

nodes.label: Decision: Package or Inline Material Include Chains in Custom KPF Materials
nodes.rationale: ss2vr_lj crashed while using include ../../materials/ND-hand.inc because a custom mod KPF cannot assume base sshock2ee material .inc files are reachable by relative path; custom materials must inline passes or package every include dependency locally.
nodes.norm_label: decision: package or inline material include chains in custom kpf materials

nodes.label: Principle: Keep Stabilized Sidequest Configs User-Facing
nodes.rationale: Once a path is confirmed live, public sample INIs should expose only user-facing tuning knobs; failed experiments/probes stay available as hidden diagnostics, default off, so stacked stale workarounds don't accumulate in the shipped config surface.
nodes.norm_label: principle: keep stabilized sidequest configs user-facing

nodes.label: Decision: Import the FreeAim View-Frame Lesson into SS2VR Pose/Aim Systems
nodes.rationale: FlatAim proved adding screen/controller offsets to world heading/pitch fails near pitch extremes (pole/roll weirdness). SS2VR had the same problem family in visible weapon bank, two-hand pitch, spread preservation, and held-object rotation; fix is to treat controller pose as a full frame (origin/forward/right/up) and express offsets as view-frame tangent offsets rather than world heading/pitch deltas. Rejected: continued sign-flip/HMD-roll-compensation layering.
nodes.norm_label: decision: import the freeaim view-frame lesson into ss2vr pose/aim systems

nodes.label: Decision: Snap-Turn Gain Is Linear Again
nodes.rationale: A dedicated F3 snap capture proved direction/pitch were stable and the only error was a 1.4x gain; set snap_turn_pixels_per_degree back to 1.0. Rejected: flipping signs again or reintroducing object-direct yaw.
nodes.norm_label: decision: snap-turn gain is linear again

nodes.label: Decision: CameraObj Remains Animation Surface, Not Proven World-Locked Visual Surface
nodes.rationale: HMD-bleed logs showed stable world/controller fields while visible CameraObj local fields moved with HMD/KEX camera, so the pose bridge is fine but the AE viewmodel consumption layer is the remaining problem. Stop treating CameraObj sign/Euler patches as the primary fix; explore a default-off world/proxy visual weapon/hand path instead.
nodes.norm_label: decision: cameraobj remains animation surface, not proven world-locked visual surface

nodes.label: Decision: FlatAim Bakes Projectile Baseline and Attaches Weapon Effects Through PointRig
nodes.rationale: Bakes proj_viewframe=1 defaults; muzzle flash and shell ejection reuse native viewmodel PointRig helpers rebased onto the freeaim world proxy pose, kept separate from projectile redirect since AE scripts spawn muzzle flash and shell eject as distinct object/effect paths from the projectile itself.
nodes.norm_label: decision: flataim bakes projectile baseline and attaches weapon effects through pointrig

nodes.label: Decision: Treat Squirrel Camera.GetFacing as Bank/Pitch/Heading
nodes.rationale: FlatAim diagnostics proved Camera.GetFacing() is (x=bank, y=pitch, z=heading), not heading-first; code that read .x as heading silently aimed relative to world-north. Use a named helper instead of raw .x/.y/.z access. Does not apply to projectile velocity vectors or controller rays, which are already world-vector form.
nodes.norm_label: decision: treat squirrel camera.getfacing as bank/pitch/heading

nodes.label: Decision: Gravity-Glove Catch Becomes a Hand-Follow Hold
nodes.rationale: After a successful pull/catch, hand the object into the existing grab/hold lane with a short hand-distance target instead of leaving it floating at a ray/beam point, reusing the proven hold/release path to minimize mission-risk writes.
nodes.norm_label: decision: gravity-glove catch becomes a hand-follow hold

nodes.label: Decision: Physical Quick-Item Proxy Uses Native Inventory Command First
nodes.rationale: First hypospray/medpatch VR use is a transient right-hand proxy model dispatching use_obj med patch after contact/dwell; real inventory stays source of truth and the proxy is presentation-only, preserving existing gameplay rules before inventing object spawning or extraction.
nodes.norm_label: decision: physical quick-item proxy uses native inventory command first

nodes.label: Decision: VR Body Should Start From Avatar/LGMM Evidence, Not Static LGMD
nodes.rationale: AE player bodies are LGMM skeletal meshes (player.bin parses as LGMM, not LGMD) and old Shock source shows avatar archetype/puppet systems; static LGMD works for hands/items/weapons but is not enough for a posed full body. Rejected: duplicating the static hand/viewmodel pipeline or a static torso/legs LGMD.
nodes.norm_label: decision: vr body should start from avatar/lgmm evidence, not static lgmd

nodes.label: Decision: OpenXR Marker Layers Use Fresh Predicted Pose, Not Pair-Locked Submitted Pose
nodes.rationale: Selection bracket and healthbar layers are independent OpenXR composition layers, not captured scene pixels, and should not inherit pair-lock's submitted/older pose; build them from freshest predicted head pose, falling back to rendered-scene then submitted stereo-pair pose only if nothing fresher exists.
nodes.norm_label: decision: openxr marker layers use fresh predicted pose, not pair-locked submitted pose

nodes.label: Decision: VR Selection Marker Must Be Mono/Pre-Eye, Not Per-Eye
nodes.rationale: Computing the bracket from the post-stereo per-eye view baked left/right IPD offsets into one shared marker, presenting as a doubled/trailing bracket; compute from the pre-eye-offset mono view instead, matching the rule already applied to aim_residual_flat. Rejected: publishing a full world-space marker contract immediately (too much risk surface) or tuning bracket smoothing/depth (hides symptom).
nodes.norm_label: decision: vr selection marker must be mono/pre-eye, not per-eye

nodes.label: Decision: Manual Reload Tier 1 Requests Native Unload/Reload
nodes.rationale: First manual reload is a pose/state detector dispatching native unload_gun/reload_gun commands rather than modifying ammo counts or weapon state directly, since KEX already owns reload legality; per-weapon visual choreography deferred until the gameplay trigger is proven.
nodes.norm_label: decision: manual reload tier 1 requests native unload/reload

nodes.label: Decision: Two-Handed Weapons Use Right-Primary, Left-Constraint Ownership
nodes.rationale: Right hand remains sole weapon owner (origin/position/roll/fire); left hand is a secondary support constraint only near the support point, matching common VR practice and avoiding two controllers writing conflicting CameraObj state. Rejected: independent dual-hand writes, or requiring per-weapon mesh support points before any testable behavior.
nodes.norm_label: decision: two-handed weapons use right-primary, left-constraint ownership

nodes.label: Decision: Gravity Glove Stays Pickup-Only Until Forced Physics Is Proven
nodes.rationale: First gravity-glove pass reuses the existing filtered physics grab lane and requires live Physics.HasPhysics/PhysState rather than forcibly registering physics on arbitrary mission objects, since forced registration can break scripts, inventory ownership, containers, doors, and mission state.
nodes.norm_label: decision: gravity glove stays pickup-only until forced physics is proven

nodes.label: Decision: Enemy Healthbar Rides Selected-Object HP, Not Native HUD Slicing
nodes.rationale: Reads HitPoints/MAX_HP from the same stabilized Squirrel-selected object that publishes ss2vr_hl, drawing the bar as a separate OpenXR quad above the bracket, because scraping the native flat HUD healthbar would inherit flat-screen alignment/depth problems.
nodes.norm_label: decision: enemy healthbar rides selected-object hp, not native hud slicing

nodes.label: Decision: Controller Tracking Owns Gameplay Frob While Native Centre Selection Becomes Fallback
nodes.rationale: Hide the native centre crosshair and clear native centre object/hover/frob globals while either hand controller is tracking, restoring native fallback only when both controllers go stale, because multiple selection systems (VR bracket, native flat HUD bracketing, centre-screen picking) were visibly active simultaneously. Rejected: visually covering the crosshair (leaves native picking active underneath).
nodes.norm_label: decision: controller tracking owns gameplay frob while native centre selection becomes fallback

nodes.label: Decision: Native Movement Proves Held KEX Actions Before Analog Axes
nodes.rationale: Publishes OpenXR stick values as ss2vr_move then sends held in-game movement actions via Debug.Command, suppressing WASD fallback, because the Squirrel reverse bridge is a safer first proof than a guessed native axis-dispatcher RVA hook; true analog speed not claimed until the KEX axis dispatcher is confirmed.
nodes.norm_label: decision: native movement proves held kex actions before analog axes

nodes.label: Decision: CameraObj Visual Pose Uses Native KEX Camera Frame in Authoritative Mode
nodes.rationale: Projectile/right-hand aim world fields stay raw and controller-authored, but in render_view_authoritative=true, visible weapon/hand CameraObj fields are produced by projecting the stable controller world pose back into the native pre-override KEX camera frame, since CameraObj is authored before the HMD-authoritative RenderView rewrite and raw HMD-local is the wrong frame when they diverge.
nodes.norm_label: decision: cameraobj visual pose uses native kex camera frame in authoritative mode

nodes.label: Decision: Add Row-Level Weighted Percent Complete to the Phase Tracker
nodes.rationale: Keep YES/BUILT/EXPLORING/NO as the human-readable status source of truth, and add a derived weighted Percent Complete column (100/75/35/0) per row so the tracker stays scannable while showing per-phase completion.
nodes.norm_label: decision: add row-level weighted percent complete to the phase tracker

nodes.label: Decision (Resolved): Left-Hand World Frob = Squirrel World-Space Scan + Engine-Frob
nodes.rationale: Card slots/switches have no collision so ray/cursor picks can't hit them, and the screen-cursor is head/camera-coupled; ships as (1) Squirrel world-space proximity scan for selection, (2) ss2vr_hl publish-back so the DLL draws the bracket, (3) writing the target into engine frob globals so native USE supplies Frobber=player for inventory checks. Rejected: ray_trace/pick_camera_probe/flat-cursor calibration, and hand-sent FrobWorldEnd (crashes or lacks Frobber).
nodes.norm_label: decision (resolved): left-hand world frob = squirrel world-space scan + engine-frob

nodes.label: Decision: Use Observed-KEX-Yaw Display-Baseline Steps for HMD-Authoritative Smooth Turn
nodes.rationale: In render_view_authoritative=true, held smooth turn must update the cached display baseline from observed KEX yaw delta (not requested joystick degrees) and keep the sample alive across short gaps, because full baseline recapture baked off-axis HMD pitch into the baseline (horizon snap) and request-based yaw had the wrong gain. Rejected: repeated full rebaseline, request-based yaw-only, and opposite-sign observed-KEX correction (all live-falsified).
nodes.norm_label: decision: use observed-kex-yaw display-baseline steps for hmd-authoritative smooth turn

nodes.label: Decision: Keep Skill Spread but Suppress View Recoil for VR Weapons
nodes.rationale: Spread: re-apply the engine's skill-based spread cone around the controller ray at projectile redirect instead of setting the raw controller ray, preserving skill balance. Recoil: never apply GunKick's view-angle kick to the HMD view (nausea hazard); express recoil via controller haptics and a transient viewmodel CameraObj kick instead. Rejected: pinpoint shots (drops skill balance) or letting native GunKick kick the view.
nodes.norm_label: decision: keep skill spread but suppress view recoil for vr weapons

nodes.label: Decision: Test Main-Menu VR Control Through DLL Navigation Bridge First
nodes.rationale: Start Phase 2.4 with a default-off DLL/controller navigation bridge instead of Squirrel or Options-RML cvar experiments, since AE main/options menus are native RmlUi running before the Squirrel layer and the Options data model is fixed, so custom ss2vr_* controls cannot bind directly. Ray-and-cursor menu interaction is deferred as polish.
nodes.norm_label: decision: test main-menu vr control through dll navigation bridge first

nodes.label: Principle: Melee Synthetic Fire Must Fail Closed
nodes.rationale: Release synthetic native fire immediately when the weapon-hand pose becomes invalid/inactive during a melee gesture, since a tracking drop during a charged swing could otherwise leave native fire held down until tracking returned or a timeout fired; real trigger input and synthetic gesture input must not fight over native fire release timing.
nodes.norm_label: principle: melee synthetic fire must fail closed

nodes.label: Decision: Keep Deliverable Requirements Visible in the Tracker
nodes.rationale: Use dedicated Google Sheet columns (HMD ONLY, MOTION CONTROLS, ROOMSCALE) to mark which tasks are required per deliverable tier, since the project now has multiple viable deliverable shapes and the tracker needs to show blocking work without overloading the simple phase/status columns.
nodes.norm_label: decision: keep deliverable requirements visible in the tracker

nodes.label: Decision: Prototype Weapon Handoff Through AE Squirrel Viewmodel
nodes.rationale: Validate the AE mod-layer path before adding more native weapon writes: a top-priority KPF probe overrides only sq_scripts/libs/viewmodel.nut and changes gun CameraObj placement, since the first-person gun is positioned every frame by Squirrel CameraObj writes. Rejected: chasing generic native movement/LOS traces, or writing native WeaponOffset/PlyrArm/creature-attachment transforms before the script path is tested.
nodes.norm_label: decision: prototype weapon handoff through ae squirrel viewmodel

nodes.label: Decision: Switch Weapon Probe From Class Replacement to Unique Squirrel Handler
nodes.rationale: The v0.2 viewmodel.nut replacement never printed and had no effect, so ship a unique sq_scripts/ss2vr_weapon_probe.nut registering a late ND.g_PlayerCore handler that writes CameraObj after Nightdive's normal WeaponHandler update, isolating loader behavior from class-replacement semantics. v0.5 absolute writes confirmed CameraObj as the correct Phase 4.2 control surface.
nodes.norm_label: decision: switch weapon probe from class replacement to unique squirrel handler

nodes.label: Decision: Weapon Aim Returns to Log-Only Carrier Identification
nodes.rationale: 0x3FCAA5 and 0x3FE22B are downstream moving-object physics/LOS, not direct weapon-aim sinks; add default-off log-only carrier probes and suppress older experimental trace/launch rewrites while they run, since pistol/laser tests didn't hit the earlier handler traces. Rejected: patching 0x3FCAA5 globally, or trusting the old handler traces without fresh evidence.
nodes.norm_label: decision: weapon aim returns to log-only carrier identification

nodes.label: Decision: Right-Hand Hitscan Takeover Rewrites Handler Trace End Only
nodes.rationale: Use the guarded FUN_1404574c0 segment-trace hook only for confirmed return RVAs 0x3EF0E7/0x3EF14E inside FUN_1403eedd0, rewriting only end.xyz while preserving KEX's original start point, range, and cell metadata, gated on right_hand_aim plus a valid weapon-hand ray, to avoid shooting around corners. Rejected: tuning FUN_14051ee80, globally rewriting all trace calls, or moving shot origin to the controller in the first prototype.
nodes.norm_label: decision: right-hand hitscan takeover rewrites handler trace end only

nodes.label: Decision: Predict Locked Stereo Pairs to Their Submit Frame
nodes.rationale: Added pair_lock_prediction_frames (default 2.0) since a locked stereo pair takes two game frames to assemble and the prior lastPredictedDisplayTime+1-period target underpredicted the first eye of a two-frame locked pair. Rejected: disabling pair lock by default, or hardcoding a larger prediction without an INI knob.
nodes.norm_label: decision: predict locked stereo pairs to their submit frame

nodes.label: Decision: Retry Authoritative RenderView as a Diagnostic, Not Baseline
nodes.rationale: render_view_authoritative=true is worth retesting after pitch-authority and quaternion fixes since it removes the KEX yaw/pitch visual round trip, but stays diagnostic-only until culling/selection/recenter are revalidated. Rejected: promoting it directly to the active baseline.
nodes.norm_label: decision: retry authoritative renderview as a diagnostic, not baseline

nodes.label: Decision: Object-Direct Angle Writes Are Yaw-Only
nodes.rationale: SS2VR reads KEX yaw from object+0x58 but reads authoritative pitch from positionData+0x12; writing pitch through FUN_140452a00 updates the object triplet, not the field SS2VR reads back, so direct writes preserve object-triplet pitch and write yaw only. Rejected: pushing HMD pitch into the object triplet, or raw-writing positionData+0x12 without a log-only validation pass first.
nodes.norm_label: decision: object-direct angle writes are yaw-only

nodes.label: Decision: Use Valid Signed-Rotation Quaternion Calibration
nodes.rationale: Individual quaternion component sign-flips are not a valid per-axis calibration when signs differ; replace with a signed rotation-vector rebuild and use the same forward-vector yaw/pitch definition for render residual/logging that game-camera aim uses. Rejected: keeping per-axis sign multipliers, or rebuilding orientation from independent Euler angles (known to cause coupled-axis bugs after large yaw).
nodes.norm_label: decision: use valid signed-rotation quaternion calibration

nodes.label: Decision: Smooth Turn Uses the KEX Accumulator, Not Object-Direct Yaw
nodes.rationale: The SS2VR-owned direct-yaw accumulator still produced jumpy held turning and pitch-down drift because KEX's canonical camera state can restore/rebase yaw and pitch on later ticks; feed KEX's normal pre-turn mouse accumulator with small analog deltas instead, keeping the pitch servo active during held turn. Rejected: continuing to tune the direct-yaw accumulator/target pitch, or treating direct-write ok=1 as sufficient proof.
nodes.norm_label: decision: smooth turn uses the kex accumulator, not object-direct yaw

nodes.label: Decision: Smooth Turn Must Not Fight UI Ray or HMD Pose History
nodes.rationale: Left/selection beam over the UI overlay made smooth turn go wild, and turning the head with/against the joystick changed turn rate, matching smooth ticks cold-starting HMD yaw history; fix is to stamp the current HMD pose as consumed instead of clearing history, and block smooth-turn queuing briefly after the selection hand hits the UI panel. Rejected: widening the direct-yaw path again, or disabling UI ray globally while turning.
nodes.norm_label: decision: smooth turn must not fight ui ray or hmd pose history

nodes.label: Decision (Superseded): Smooth Turn Owns Its Held-Stick Yaw Target
nodes.rationale: An SS2VR-owned yaw accumulator with pitch mouse-pixel suppression on the same tick, tried after object-direct writes proved callable but still let KEX yaw/pitch jump around it; using current KEX yaw/pitch as rolling baseline preserved the corrupted state being avoided. Superseded by the KEX-accumulator decision.
nodes.norm_label: decision (superseded): smooth turn owns its held-stick yaw target

nodes.label: Principle: Use Original SS2 Mod Data as Semantic Reference Only
nodes.rationale: Mine original SS2/NewDark and NixOS mod material for names, property semantics, message flow, and option concepts, but never treat original/NewDark Squirrel services, DML properties, or cam_ext.cfg commands as callable AE native APIs without Ghidra/runtime confirmation. Track confidence as original-reference -> AE mod-layer confirmed -> AE native binary confirmed; only the last graduates into ADDRESS_REGISTRY.md.
nodes.norm_label: principle: use original ss2 mod data as semantic reference only

nodes.label: Principle: Keep SEH Native-Call Wrappers POD-Only
nodes.rationale: Any new SEH wrapper for unsafe native calls must be a tiny raw-call helper taking only POD/raw pointer values and returning a simple status; logging, config mutation, std::string, STL containers, and other destructor-bearing objects must stay outside __try/__except, since MSVC rejects __try in functions requiring C++ object unwinding (C2712).
nodes.norm_label: principle: keep seh native-call wrappers pod-only

nodes.label: Decision: Stage Native Input Backend, Keep Explicit Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Add input_backend=native and route only confirmed actions (fire via FUN_140068840, frob via FUN_14048b4f0) through native game-thread calls; movement/jump/crouch/inventory keep keyboard fallback with explicit logs until the real KEX axis dispatcher is found. Rejected: replacing all controls with guessed native calls at once.
nodes.norm_label: decision: stage native input backend, keep explicit fallbacks

nodes.label: Decision: Direct Snap Uses Object-Direct Angles Only
nodes.rationale: Direct snap must use the object-direct angle setter and report success only when angle readback moves by the expected yaw delta, because a prior log loaded direct-yaw mode but actually wrote through the already-falsified generic updater, with readback unchanged and KEX yaw jumping wildly afterward.
nodes.norm_label: decision: direct snap uses object-direct angles only

nodes.label: Decision: Direct Snap Replaces Same-Tick KEX Yaw
nodes.rationale: Keep direct snap post-PlayerTurnTilt but compute its yaw target from pre-snap KEX yaw, not post-KEX yaw, since if KEX/original yaw moves during the same tick, afterReal-requested can inherit a bad intermediate yaw while before-requested avoids it.
nodes.norm_label: decision: direct snap replaces same-tick kex yaw

nodes.label: Principle: Promote Useful Hook-Map Data into Compact RE Docs
nodes.rationale: Keep future-hook-map.md as the long historical scratchpad, but route curated evidence/confidence/interpretations into RE_FINDINGS.md and compact RVA/global lookups into ADDRESS_REGISTRY.md, since the scratchpad mixes confirmed addresses, static leads, and falsified experiments and future work needs fast access without re-reading every probe.
nodes.norm_label: principle: promote useful hook-map data into compact re docs

nodes.label: Principle: Use Spreadsheet Phase IDs in Project Docs
nodes.rationale: Use PROJECT_PHASES.md and the SS2 VR mod Google Sheet as the canonical task numbering system, adding phase/task IDs to test logs, decisions, hypotheses, and handoffs, because the project has several parallel tracks and numbered IDs make clear which problem a note belongs to.
nodes.norm_label: principle: use spreadsheet phase ids in project docs

nodes.label: Decision: Reset Baseline to One Camera Authority
nodes.rationale: Use render_view_authoritative=false, hmd_aim=true, hmd_pitch=true, suppress_render_yaw_pitch=true as the clean baseline, since KEX culling, KEX picking, and the visible HMD view need to agree before controller aim can be judged. Rejected: continuing to stack fixes on split-camera/display-authoritative mode.
nodes.norm_label: decision: reset baseline to one camera authority

nodes.label: Principle: Split INI Parser by Section
nodes.rationale: Parse each ss2vr.ini section in its own small helper instead of extending one large else-if chain, since adding weapon visual keys pushed MSVC into C1061 (blocks nested too deeply); section-local parsers preserve behavior while making future INI options safer to add and audit.
